topics.title: Creamy Layer for SC-ST Quotas
bullets: The Centre has filed an affidavit before the Supreme Court opposing the introduction of the "creamy layer" concept for reservations for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) .
The government argued that the historical disadvantages faced by these communities cannot be equated with mere economic backwardness .
It also contended that altering reservation policies falls within the domain of Parliament, not the courts . Background –

Reservation is a system of affirmative action in India that provides preferential access to education, government jobs, and political representation for socially and educationally backward communities.
The policy aims to correct historical injustices and ensure equal participation of marginalized groups in public life .
It is a constitutional mandate under Articles 15(4), 15(5), 16(4), and 16(4A) of the Constitution.
Article 15(4) empowers the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, including SCs and STs.
Article 16(4) provides for reservation in public employment for backward classes that are not adequately represented in State services.
These provisions are enabling provisions, allowing the State to take affirmative action, but not mandating it.
Under Article 341, the President notifies the list of Scheduled Castes in consultation with the Governor of the concerned State.
Under Article 342, the President notifies the list of Scheduled Tribes similarly.
Once notified, these lists can only be modified by an Act of Parliament – no other authority, including courts, can alter them .
SCs are communities that have historically faced the practice of untouchability and social discrimination .
They were identified based on their historical and social disadvantages, not just economic conditions .
The Constitution recognises the unique nature of discrimination faced by SCs, which is distinct from economic backwardness.
STs are identified by their distinct cultures, geographical isolation, and social and economic backwardness .
They are communities that have remained isolated from mainstream society and have distinct languages, customs, and traditions.
STs face challenges related to geographical remoteness, lack of access to education, and economic marginalization.
OBCs are identified primarily through a combination of social, educational, and economic disadvantages .
SCs and STs are identified based on historical factors – untouchability for SCs and geographical isolation for STs .
The "creamy layer" concept was developed for OBCs to exclude the economically advanced sections from reservation benefits . Creamy Layer –
The "creamy layer" is a concept used to exclude socially and economically advanced individuals within backward classes from reservation benefits.
It was first introduced by the Supreme Court in the 1992 Indra Sawhney (Mandal) case .
The concept ensures that reservation benefits reach the most marginalized sections within backward communities.
In the landmark Indra Sawhney judgment, the Supreme Court upheld reservations for OBCs but introduced the creamy layer test .
The Court expressly confined the creamy layer concept to OBCs, stating it "has no relevance in the case of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes" .
The judgment recognized that economic advancement does not necessarily eliminate social backwardness for SCs and STs.
The current income limit for determining the OBC creamy layer at the central level is ₹8 lakh per annum .
This limit has been a subject of debate, with demands to raise it (e.g., to ₹15 lakh) to keep more families within the reservation net .
Notably, income from salaries and agricultural land is usually excluded from this calculation to prevent penalising lower- rung employees .
In the Ashoka Kumar Thakur case (2008), the Supreme Court clarified that the creamy layer principle does not apply to SCs and STs for the purpose of reservation .
The Court held that the concept was developed specifically for OBCs, and its extension to SCs/STs would require legislative action .
This judgment reaffirmed the distinct basis for SC/ST reservations.
2004 (E.V. Chinnaiah): A 5-judge bench ruled that SCs form a homogenous group under Article 341, barring states from sub- classification or sub-quotas .
2024 : In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh, A 7-judge Constitution Bench (6:1 majority) overruled this, granting states power to sub-classify SCs to benefit more backward sub-groups .
States cannot sub-classify arbitrarily; they must justify decisions with quantifiable, empirical data proving under-representation of specific sub-castes . Recent News –
The government was responding to a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) politician and advocate Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay .
The petition argued that affluent families within SC and ST categories are monopolising reservation benefits, leading to "elite capture" .
It sought the implementation of income-based preferences across all reserved categories, including OBCs and EWS.
The petition relied on the August 2024 Supreme Court judgment (State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh) that permitted the sub- classification of SCs and STs .
In that case, four of the seven judges on the Constitution Bench suggested extending the creamy layer principle to these groups .
The petition sought to exclude socially and economically advanced individuals from reservation benefits. Centre’s Stand –
SCs, the government stated, "face historical disadvantage" stemming from the practice of untouchability .
STs are identified by their "distinct cultures, geographical isolation and backwardness" .
In contrast, OBCs are identified primarily through a combination of social, educational and economic disadvantages .

The government emphasised that the main objective of SC and ST reservations is to achieve social equality and justice, overcome historical discrimination, and ensure inclusive participation in public life .
The affidavit stated that discrimination against these communities "does not happen on the basis of economic conditions" .
Therefore, economic progress alone cannot eliminate the social disadvantages faced by these communities.
Under Articles 341 and 342, the President notifies the lists of SCs and STs, and only Parliament can modify them .
It is "not open to State Governments or courts or tribunals or any other authority to modify, amend or alter" these lists .
The petition's demand for income-based preferences requires a legislative mandate, not judicial intervention.
The government argued that courts cannot direct the executive to implement a particular policy "on the ground that a better, fairer or wiser alternative is available" .
The judiciary cannot step into the shoes of the legislature to dictate public policy .
Framing policies on reservations requires a holistic review, empirical data, and legislative mandate .
The Centre argued that the petition is not maintainable under Article 32 of the Constitution .
The petition fails to demonstrate any infringement of fundamental rights .
Calling the petition "misconceived" and devoid of merit, the government urged the Supreme Court to dismiss it .

topics.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkey Deal
bullets: On 7 August 2026, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" in the holy city of Mecca, creating a mutual defence alliance among three major Muslim- majority nations .
The pact stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries shall be regarded as an attack against all three – a clause similar to NATO's Article 5 .
The agreement was signed by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Background –
Saudi Arabia is home to Islam's holiest sites, one of the world's top oil exporters, and holds significant financial and diplomatic weight .
Turkey has NATO's second-largest military and a rapidly growing defence industry, particularly in drones and combat systems .
Pakistan is the only Muslim-majority country possessing nuclear weapons and has a large, battle-hardened military .
The agreement brings together complementary strengths: Saudi Arabia's wealth, Turkey's technology and industrial capacity, and Pakistan's manpower and nuclear deterrence .
All three nations are strategic allies of the United States but have grown increasingly concerned about the reliability of Washington's security umbrella .
The pact builds on existing bilateral military ties between Saudi Arabia-Pakistan (September 2025) and Turkey-Pakistan .
The agreement comes amid a regional war that has seen Iranian attacks on Gulf states since the US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February 2026 .
Iran and its allies have fired on Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman, Jordan, and disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea .
Saudi Arabia has been repeatedly targeted by Iranian missiles and Houthi drone strikes, threatening its oil exports and development plans .
Israel has expanded military operations across the region since October 2023, including invading southern Lebanon, seizing Syrian territory, and launching two air campaigns against Iran .
Israeli strikes have reached at least six countries across the region, including a September 2025 strike on Hamas leaders in Doha, Qatar .

Turkish interests are increasingly at odds with Israel, particularly over Syria, where Ankara wants a strong central government while Israel has occupied additional territory . September 2025 Bilateral Pact –
In September 2025, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a bilateral mutual defence agreement that similarly declared an attack on either nation as an attack on both .
Pakistan has deployed about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones, and an air-defence system to the kingdom .
Saudi analysts suggested Riyadh could activate the bilateral pact if directly drawn into the Iran conflict, accelerating momentum toward the trilateral framework.
Pakistan has trained more than 8,200 Saudi Arabian soldiers since 1967 and has decades of military cooperation with the kingdom .
The two countries have held numerous joint military exercises and Pakistan has provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades .
Saudi Arabia is a major purchaser of Turkish drones, with a 2023 agreement described as Ankara's largest defence export contract .
Turkey and Pakistan have exchanged warships and training aircraft, and Islamabad uses many weapons systems and UAVs manufactured by Ankara .
The three countries have run a formal defence-industrial forum since at least 2022, laying the groundwork for the current agreement . Recent News –
On 7 August 2026, the agreement was signed in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, at Al-Safa Palace .
The ceremony was attended by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif .
Sharif arrived in Saudi Arabia a day earlier, accompanied by powerful army chief Asim Munir, and performed the Umrah pilgrimage in Mecca.
The pact states that an armed attack against any one of the three countries shall be regarded as an attack against all three .
The agreement is "intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression" and provides for the enhancement of all aspects of defence cooperation among the three states .
It is "purely defensive in nature" and does not target any specific country, according to Turkish officials .
The agreement is likely to allow joint military exercises and training, technology transfers, and intelligence sharing .
It builds on the existing Saudi-Pakistan bilateral pact signed in September 2025 and expands it to include Turkey .
The pact does not specify what military action each country would be obliged to take if another were attacked .
Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif called the pact a "shield of peace" for the region and a "historic endeavour" serving the interests of all three nations .
Turkish President Erdogan said the agreement is "based on collective deterrence" and "does not target any country" .
Saudi Arabia's Rayed Krimly stated the pact is "not linked to nuclear ambitions or an arms race" and does not represent a "military axis or sectarian/religious bloc" .
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office declined to comment on the agreement .
Israeli officials have increasingly identified Turkey as a potential strategic threat as their interests collide in Syria .
Former Israeli PM Naftali Bennett previously described Turkey as "the new Iran" and accused Ankara of seeking a "hostile Sunni axis with nuclear Pakistan" . NATO –
NATO is a transatlantic military alliance of 32 countries from Europe and North America, formed to guarantee the freedom and security of its members through political and military means .
The alliance was established on 4 April 1949 with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C. .
It was created as a collective defence alliance against the perceived threat of Soviet expansion in post-WWII Europe .
The founding members included the United States, Canada, and 10 European nations: Belgium, Britain, Denmark, France, Iceland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, and Portugal .
The alliance has expanded significantly over time, with key enlargements occurring in 1952 (Greece and Turkey) , 1955 (West Germany) , 1982 (Spain) , and after the Cold War in 1999, 2004, and 2009 .
The newest members are Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024) , who joined after previously pursuing a policy of military non- alignment .
The "core" of the NATO treaty is Article 5, which states that an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all members .
It has been invoked only once in NATO's history, following the 9/11 terrorist attacks on the United States in 2001 .

The obligation is not automatic military action; each member decides what "action it deems necessary" to assist an attacked ally, which could range from political support to the use of armed force . Passage: On 7 August 2026, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, creating a new trilateral security arrangement with a collective-defence clause. The pact provides that an armed attack on one of the three countries will be treated as an attack on all, drawing comparisons with NATO’s Article 5. The agreement was signed amid heightened regional insecurity following the 2026 Iran conflict and growing concerns over dependence on external security guarantees. The trilateral pact built on the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement already concluded between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in September 2025. Earlier in 2026, Pakistani fighter and support aircraft were deployed to Saudi Arabia under that bilateral arrangement. Türkiye had separately been negotiating to join a wider security framework, with a draft trilateral agreement reportedly under discussion since early 2026. Source: The Hindu
